title: Process Transactions in Order
real_world_story: A banking system receives transaction requests continuously. Transactions must be processed in exactly the same order in which they were received.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Transaction requests received by the banking system
real_world_connection.target_represents: Transactions in the order they should be processed
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: A queue that processes the earliest received transaction first

problem_statement: Given N transaction IDs in the order they are received, process them using FIFO ordering and print the transaction IDs in the order in which they are processed.
task: Process all transaction requests in the same order in which they were received.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of transactions. The second line contains N space-separated transaction IDs.
output_format: Print the transaction IDs in their processing order separated by spaces.

examples.explanation: Transactions are processed in the same order in which they entered the system.
The first transaction received is processed first, followed by the remaining transactions.

expected_algorithm.name: Queue
expected_algorithm.reason: A queue follows First-In-First-Out ordering, which matches the required transaction-processing order.

hint: Insert each transaction into a queue.
Remove transactions from the front of the queue.
Process each transaction in the order it was inserted.
real_world_takeaway: Queue operations are useful when banking systems must process incoming requests fairly and maintain their arrival order.
